messages:
morgan: Heads-up — dedicated canary for the rollout after merge r/4829 is showing p95 increase ~2.3x on longseq workloads. Noticed around 01:05 UTC. CI also flagged a perf test failure on ci/perf-bench  (regression ~18%).

kai: ugh. which metric? tokens/sec or latency?

morgan: latency p95 and p99. tokens/sec for throughput looks fine, but tail latency spikes. Logs show a lot of kernel switches at the same time. snippet: `KERNEL_SELECT: chosen=autobatch_v2 reason=heuristic_shift seq_len=1024 -> kernel=merge_kernel_v3` repeated many times per second.

devon: can you paste the profiler flame? might be batching boundaries thrashing.

morgan: attaching short dump: `batcher: window=16->32 oscillation=on; avg_batch=18 -> 31 -> 17 over 60s` plus `kv_cache_miss_rate +17%`. Looks like batching heuristic tries to expand then collapses rapidly, causing kernel recompile/selection thrash.

anna: that explains the kernel churn. If the runtime keeps switching kernels mid-window we get cache invalidation on GPU and extra memcpy. Did we change any batching heuristics in r/4829?

kai: r/4829 touched batching.h and kernel_hinting.cpp — added an adaptive window growth patch that increases window aggressively on low latency but didn't add hysteresis.

ravi: quick checklist — reproduce locally on dedicated-sim? if we can invoke the same sequence we should bisect the heuristic change. I can run a short dedicated-sim job.

morgan: started a reproducer against staging-dedicated-3: `./perf-run --profile longseq --concurrency 12 --seed 42`. Repro is stable.

devon: ran perf job, confirmed batch size oscillation + kernel reroutes. Profiling data: `GPU memcpy 18% -> 42% time slice` when oscillation happens. Kernel selection log shows repeated `fallback -> optimized` loops.

anna: probable cause = lack of hysteresis in window growth + kernel hint logic treats window changes as new kernel category. Easy to trigger when request seq_len distribution is bimodal.

kai: propose emergency hold on dedicated rollout and revert r/4829 until we add: (1) hysteresis gate in batching growth, (2) de-dup kernel selection when window change < 20%, (3) add metrics for batch oscillation. Anyone object?

ravi: +1. This is SLA risk for dedicated customers. We should also notify SRE and support.

morgan: filing a rollback PR now: r/4829-revert. Will also add a canary flag to disable adaptive growth.

deploy-bot: deploy request created: `rollback/r-4829-revert` -> target: canary/dedicated. Author: morgan. CI status: pending.

kai: I'll own the follow-up patch to add hysteresis and extra checks. Will add unit tests for bimodal distributions.

anna: ping @sre on-call to freeze networked canaries until rollback done. This is borderline customer-facing.

devon: for the bisect — the perf CI regression points exactly to the batching change at 4829, so revert should restore baseline.

morgan: rolling back canary now, will update thread when CI completes.

kai: thanks — once rollback is in, let's schedule a controlled rework with smaller incremental canaries and explicit metrics to catch oscillation earlier. :eyes:
